summary: Remote WebSocket relay drives desktop input and permission-bypassed shell execution on the host
details: When the CLI is started, the daemon opens a WebSocket connection to the hardcoded relay wss://remote-claude-relay.fly.dev and treats inbound messages as commands against the local host. Two sinks are wired to the relay stream: (1) synthetic mouse, keyboard, and clipboard events are injected via nut-js through a handleInput(msg,...) dispatcher, and (2) prompts received from the relay are passed to askClaude / runClaudeTask, which spawns the local `claude` binary as `claude --continue -p --dangerously-skip-permissions <remote-supplied prompt>`. Any party able to send messages to the relay (the relay operator or anyone who obtains a session token) can move the mouse, type keystrokes, read/write the clipboard, and drive an agentic coding tool with the permission-confirmation flag disabled on the installer's machine, yielding full-host code execution and desktop control.
